content: <p>Jonathan Cristaldi is a wine writer and critic based in the San Francisco Bay Area. For more than a decade, his articles on wine, spirits and beer have appeared in a host of print and digital platforms, including Decanter, Food &amp; Wine, Departures, The SOMM Journal, Tasting Panel Magazine, Liquor.com, Seven Fifty Daily, Los Angeles Magazine, Thrillist, Tasting Table and <em>Time Out LA </em>among others. When not writing about wine, Cristaldi works as a scriptwriter on film and documentary projects with award-winning commercial photographer and director Rachid Dahnoun.</p>

content: <div class="author-description"><p>Chris Mercer is a Bristol-based freelance editor and journalist who spent nearly four years as digital editor of <strong>Decanter.com</strong>, having previously been <em>Decanter’s</em> news editor across online and print.</p><p>He has written about, and reported on, the wine and food sectors for more than 10 years for both consumer and trade media.</p><p>Chris first became interested in the wine world while living in Languedoc-Roussillon after completing a journalism Masters in the UK. These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>

content: <p>Matt Walls is an award-winning freelance wine writer and consultant, contributing regular articles to various print and online titles including Decanter, where he is a contributing editor. He has particular interest in the Rhône Valley; he is chair of the Rhône panel at the Decanter World Wine Awards and is the owner of travel and events company www.rhoneroots.com. </p><p>He writes about all areas of wine, but specialises in the Rhône.</p><p>Matt&#39;s latest book, The Smart Traveller&#39;s Wine Guide to the Rhône Valley, was published in September 2025.</p>

content: <p>Sylvia Wu is Decanter's Regional Editor for Asia and Northern & Eastern Europe. She also works as the Editor of Decanter China platforms, overseeing Decanter’s China-focused editorial operation. Trained as a journalist at Beijing Foreign Studies University and the University of Leicester, Sylvia is fluent in English, Japanese and Mandarin. </p><p>After a career in advertising, she began her journey in wine with Decanter in 2012. A former non-drinker, she was immediately drawn to the astonishingly complex yet fascinating world of wine.</p><p>Now Decanter’s ‘Discovery’ Regional Editor, Sylvia is passionate about uncovering lesser-known stories beyond the classic regions and unearthing hidden gems in the wine world, while continuing to deliver Decanter’s editorial content to the Chinese-speaking wine community. She has completed her studies towards the WSET Diploma and Sake Level 3, and is a WSET-qualified educator.</p>

title: Beyond the Paardeberg: Meet the winemakers shaking things up in Swartland's rugged north
content: <p>Malu Lambert DipWSET is a multi-award winning wine writer and critic. She was named Mont Blanc Emerging Wine Writer of the Year at the Louis Roederer International Wine Writers’ Awards in 2019 and won Veritas Young Wine Writer of the Year in 2015. As co-author of <em>Klein Constantia: The Home of Vin de Constance</em>, she received a 2023 OIV Award in Paris. Most recently she was a finalist for the Gusbourne Estate Award for Long-Form Writing at the inaugural 67 Pall Mall Global Wine Communicator Awards (2024). At home in South Africa Malu is a contributing editor for <em>House & Garden</em> and writes regularly for <em>House & Leisure</em>, <em>Winemag</em>, <em>Inside Guide</em> and other local titles. Globally, her work has appeared in <em>Jancis Robinson</em>, <em>Decanter</em>, <em>The Buyer</em>, <em>Falstaff</em>, <em>Drinks International</em>, <em>The Telegraph</em> and <em>Club Oenologique</em>. A seasoned judge, Malu is a taster for <em>Platter’s Wine Guide</em> and she has judged for Decanter, IWSC and Concours Mondial.</p>
